title: Night ops clipboard — annotations and followups
body:
Quick summary (overnight shift, 00:00–08:00 PDT)

- Scope: routine oncall window covering hosted inference APIs and dedicated capacity pools for us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Quiet for first half of shift; spike started ~03:14 when a backend deploy (infra autoscaling change) caused repeated scaling failures and downstream 503s.

Incidents and observations
1) Primary symptom: sudden increase in 5xxs from inference-gateway (api-frontend) hitting 503/502. Synthetic traffic checks showed increased tail latency rising from 150ms -> 1.8s on 99th pct. Error rates peaked ~03:22.
   - Incident ref: INC-2027-546 (created by PagerDuty trigger).
   - Root cause (interim): autoscaler policy change introduced at 02:58 (PR 3456) reduced headroom for new pods and caused rapid scale attempts; combined with an aggressively low gracePeriod on health-checks, causing churn.
   - Mitigation applied: rolled back autoscaler policy to previous commit at 03:40, adjusted cluster autoscaler back-to-original target at 03:44. Error rate began to recover by 03:51.

2) Secondary symptom: cache warmup mismatch for prefix-cache service (kv-cache). Several long-tail requests experienced cold-KV misses -> downstream compute spike. Observed heavier-than-expected cold starts when traffic was routed to a smaller pool during the autoscaler flapping window.
   - Observed by: Priya (metrics) and Oscar (logs).
   - Mitigation: temporarily increased cache-replica target to 2 for affected ASG at 04:05 (manual override). This reduced cold miss ratio by ~60% within 10 minutes.

3) Failover activity: regional failover to us-west-1 was initiated by the routing policy when eu-central-1's dedicated nodes hit quota. Failover was successful but increased cross-region latency for a subset of customers. We opened a customer note (internal) to track potential impact.

Action items and follow-ups (assigned)
- Update autoscaler runbook: document rollback steps for the specific policy change introduced in PR 3456, and include verification queries for synthetic latency checks. Owner: Liam Chen. Due: 2027-10-09. Linked: JIRA-OPS-2987.
- Add pre-deploy canary that validates cache warmup behavior under reduced pool sizes (synthetic scenario). Owner: Priya Desai. Due: 2027-10-14.
- Add a short-term guard in the routing layer to avoid cross-region failover for customers with strict geo requirements unless manual approval is set. Owner: Product/Platform (tagging for follow-up). Owner point-of-contact: Oscar Martinez. Due: 2027-10-21.
- Create a compact runbook appendix for KV-cache replica scaling with concrete PromQL alerts and remediation commands (kubectl patch examples). Owner: Aisha Khan. Due: 2027-10-12.

Runbook edits proposed (quick notes)
- Autoscaler section: add explicit checklist to confirm new policy doesn't change minNodes/minReadyPercent. Add rollback CLI snippet and exact metrics to watch (api-frontend 5xx rate, deployment rollout status, cluster-autoscaler events).
- Cache warmup: add a short test harness to simulate small pool warmup and measure cold-miss ratio; include a threshold to block policy changes if cold-miss > 25% in a 5-min window.
- Failover: concrete decision matrix for automatic failover vs manual escalation when quota-related failover is the trigger. Add guidance on customer-facing comms.

Metrics snapshots (high-level)
- api-frontend 5xx rate: baseline 0.02% -> peak 1.8% during incident.
- p99 latency (tokenized requests): baseline 150ms -> 1.8s peak.
- kv-cache cold miss ratio: baseline 6% -> 38% during peak.
- scale event count: 6 scale failures recorded between 03:00–03:30.

Communication notes
- Slack thread: #sre-ops channel (linked above). Primary incident channel created at 03:16 and stood down at 04:30.
- Internal customer note drafted and shared with CS for customers in eu-central-1 that may have experienced degraded performance (ask: CS to proactively reach out to top 10 accounts).
- Postmortem: will be drafted after follow-ups are closed; target first-draft by 2027-10-11.

To-do for incoming shift (next handoff)
- Verify rollback and autoscaler policy remains at the stable commit; check cluster-autoscaler metrics for the last 12h.
- Run the new synthetic warmup test (PR to be merged by Priya) against a staging ASG and report results.
- Validate no further cross-region failovers occurred overnight and reconcile with routing logs.
- Confirm JIRA-OPS-2987 is updated with the status and link PR #3456 to the ticket.

Notes to self / informal observations
- During the spike, the telemetry dashboard was slow; consider a cached snapshot widget for rapid triage.
- We should re-evaluate our default health-check gracePeriod assumptions for the heavier LLM backends — aggressive settings get us into a restart loop under cold caches.
- Small reminder: the emergency rollback play needs a one-liner that non-core SREs can run without digging into repo branches (i.e., a short curl/kubectl sequence).

Unresolved questions
- Was there any correlated storage IO pressure at the same time? We saw occasional EBS latency blips but not enough to be conclusive. Action: infra team to check EBS metrics for ASG nodes.
- Did any customer usage patterns (long token context jobs) amplify the cold-start effect? Action: product analytics to check large-context job prevalence during window.

Appendix: quick commands used (for documentation)
- Rollback autoscaler: git revert <commit-hash-of-3456> && kubectl apply -f cluster-autoscaler.yml
- Force cache-replica scale: kubectl patch hpa kv-cache -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'
- Check rollout: kubectl rollout status deploy/api-frontend -n prod

Last remark: handoff to morning crew at 08:00 PDT. Please ping me on Slack if any of the follow-ups need clarification — leaving a short checklist in the ticket JIRA-OPS-2987 so morning lead can reassign if needed.

-- Aisha

(Notes: informal, rough-cut. Will be cleaned into the postmortem doc and runbook patches after assigned follow-ups are completed.)
